analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: The best mega-cap setup on the board: a trillion-dollar name consolidating 1.2% below its high with RSI 51 while every AI mega-cap breaks down.

financials.summary: The incretin franchise moved Lilly from a large-cap pharma to one of the fastest-growing companies of any size at scale. Revenue growth was driven by tirzepatide across both diabetes and obesity indications, with volume expansion finally catching up to demand after multi-year supply constraints. Operating leverage was dramatic - revenue grew faster than the cost base, so earnings grew far faster than sales, and margins expanded even while the company was spending aggressively on manufacturing capacity expansion and a deep late-stage pipeline. Cash generation funded that capex build plus a rising dividend.
highlights: Revenue growth ~+55.5% YoY - extraordinary for a company of this scale
EPS growth ~+169.9% YoY - operating leverage on a fixed cost base
Incretin franchise (tirzepatide) the primary growth engine across diabetes and obesity
Heavy manufacturing capex to relieve multi-year supply constraints
Margin expansion despite record R&D and capacity spending

accomplishments: Became one of the very few $1T-plus market-cap healthcare companies
Scaled incretin manufacturing capacity to convert backlog demand into revenue
Broadened obesity/cardiometabolic label coverage and reimbursement access
Advanced an oral incretin candidate toward commercialisation, addressing the injectable bottleneck

journey_52w.summary: Roughly doubled over the past year - from $621 at the 52-week low to $1,235 at the high - as supply caught up with demand and the obesity market's addressable size was repeatedly revised upward. Crucially, the last few weeks have been a tight sideways consolidation rather than a blow-off, which is why RSI is 51 at a price 1.2% off the high.

financials.summary: Howmet supplies engineered fasteners, engine airfoils, forged wheels and structural castings into commercial aerospace, defense and transportation. The year was defined by mix and pricing: engine-products revenue grew fastest and carries the best margins, and long-term agreements let Howmet pass through both inflation and value. Operating margin expanded meaningfully, which is why EPS grew roughly four times faster than revenue. Free cash flow supported debt reduction, a growing dividend and buybacks.

financials.period: Most recent disclosed fiscal year (first full year as a public company)
financials.summary: Two businesses in one. Launch is the mature, dominant piece - the highest cadence of orbital launches globally, with reusability driving a cost-per-kilogram advantage no competitor has matched, serving commercial, government and internal Starlink missions. Starlink is the growth engine: a satellite broadband network converting enormous upfront constellation capex into recurring consumer, enterprise, maritime, aviation and government subscription revenue. The financial profile is therefore capex-heavy with rapidly growing recurring revenue - the central question for investors is the timing of sustained profitability as constellation spending continues. Treat all specific figures with care: as a recent listing, the reporting history is short, and the live numbers on the TradingView widget below are the authority.

journey_52w.summary: A short and painful public history. The stock listed and ran to $211.39, then round-tripped the entire move to close today at $116.41 - 44.9% off the high, 22% below its 50-day ($148.74), and barely above its all-time low of $113.50 with RSI at 23 and three-month momentum of -27.7%. This is the standard post-IPO deflation pattern - initial scarcity bid, then supply and reality - made worse by the fact that it is happening during a broad unwind of speculative space and AI names (RKLB -57.5%, LUNR -72.9%, RGTI -74.2%).
